\chapter{Binary Search on Arrays}
\label{ch:binary_search}

\begin{tcolorbox}[enhanced, colback=white, colframe=secondaryblue, boxrule=1pt, arc=2mm]
\textbf{\large\textcolor{primaryblue}{Sorted data answers ``where is $x$?'' in $\bigO{\log n}$: bounds, counting, nearest values and prefix sums --- the basic toolkit every array chapter uses.}}
\end{tcolorbox}

\chapterfacts{1000}{1600}{4}{8}{30}

\begin{plannedbox}[Planned Contents --- this chapter is not written yet]
\textbf{Part A --- Lessons}
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*, label=\textbf{A\arabic*.}, itemsep=1pt]
    \item The monotone predicate and the loop invariant: ``everything left of $lo$ is false, everything from $hi$ is true''
    \item \texttt{lower\_bound} and \texttt{upper\_bound}: counting elements in a value range
    \item Sort, then search: answering many queries against a sorted copy
    \item Binary search on prefix sums of non-negative arrays and on prefix maxima
    \item A first search on the answer over a small range (the full technique is the binary search book)
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{Part B --- Patterns} (with the two solved problems of each pattern)
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*, label=\textbf{P\arabic*.}, itemsep=1pt]
    \item \textbf{Counting with bounds} --- Maximum Count of Positive Integer and Negative Integer {\small\color{darkgray}(LeetCode 2529)}, Find Target Indices After Sorting Array {\small\color{darkgray}(LeetCode 2089)}
    \item \textbf{Nearest values in sorted arrays} --- Find K Closest Elements {\small\color{darkgray}(LeetCode 658)}, Maximum Distance Between a Pair of Values {\small\color{darkgray}(LeetCode 1855)}
    \item \textbf{Binary search on prefix sums} --- Eating Queries {\small\color{darkgray}(CF 1676E)}, Scuza {\small\color{darkgray}(CF 1742E)}
    \item \textbf{A first search on the answer} --- Special Array With X Elements Greater Than or Equal X {\small\color{darkgray}(LeetCode 1608)}, Sum of Mutated Array Closest to Target {\small\color{darkgray}(LeetCode 1300)}
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{Connections.} Rotated arrays, peaks, binary search on the answer, ternary, real-valued, interactive and offline binary search are the \textit{Binary Search} book.
